contexts.text: Spirits who are in mere knowledge are in so cold a life...
(This poisoner) became cold; thus was among the cold infernals.
Cold and heat () = the state of the man who is being regenerated, which is such as to the reception of faith and charity; cold = no faith and charity. Explained.
When he returns into the body again he is again in cold.
Cold = no love, or no charity and faith. Illustrated.

The alternations of those who are to be regenerated are likened to cold and heat, but those of the regenerate to summer and winter. Explained... For the man who is being regenerated begins from cold...
(The meritorious) are cold, and try to warm themselves by sawing... AC 2027:2. AC 4943.
When I got near that misty rock, cold met me, which invaded the lower part of the back.
That (infernal) fire is extinguished, and turned into cold.
In course of time charity begins to grow cold.

To this heat the opposite is cold; in this live the infernals; their cold is from the evils in which they are... and the further they are from good, the greater is their cold... Their heat is turned into cold as soon as they perceive anything of good.
They who are in Hell are in... cold... In proportion as the infernals are in hatred and thence in falsity, they are in darkness and in cold... Cold there, has hatred in it.
Lest one come into a state of too much cold. Signified. There is cold when there is aversion for these (goods), which is induced by the loves of self.
A cold breathing into my forehead.

In the day the heat devoured me, and the cold in the night () = temptations. Heat and cold = too much love, and none of it, thus the two extremes... Spiritual cold is no love... Cold, however, does not signify the deprivation of all love, but the deprivation of spiritual and celestial love... When man is deprived of this love, the love of self and of the world is kindled; this love is relatively cold, and also becomes cold, not only with man while he lives in the body, but also when he comes into the other life. If, while he lives in the body, the love of self and of the world is taken away from him, he grows so cold that he has scarcely any life; in like manner if he is driven to think holily about heavenly and Divine things. In the other life, if he approaches Heaven, his fire and heat are turned into cold, which is the more intense the nearer that he approaches... This cold is what is meant by the gnashing of teeth.
They who have known truths, and have confirmed them, yet have lived a life of evil, appear in a snowy light, but cold.
Spirits who infuse unclean colds, like those of ague.
The ultimates which are with man, are comparatively sluggish, and thence cold.
This Spirit... was cold, as was plainly felt from his afflatus; which was a sign of merely natural lumen...
The Spirits say that they know them by their cold...
Although their faces are fiery, they are cold...
When in externals, man... grows warm from the world, and grows cold to Heaven, unless it is as the world. AC 9278:5.
Without that heat... the internal of man would grow cold.
In proportion as the internal man is closed towards Heaven to the Lord, he is in cold and thick darkness as to those things which are of Heaven.
They who are in self-love, and in the persuasion of intelligence and wisdom from self, are in such cold and thick darkness.
Truths outside the Heavens shine coldly... Wherefore when the light of Heaven falls upon that cold light, it disappears.
This infernal heat is turned into intense cold when heat from Heaven flows in...
Melancthon... appears clothed with bearskin on account of the cold.
A cup of cold water = something of truth.
Neither cold nor hot () = that those who are such sometimes deny, and at other times acknowledge, that the Word is Divine and holy.
I would thou wert cold or hot = that it is better for them either from the heart to deny the holy things of the Word and of the Church, or from the heart to acknowledge them. AR 204.
The Angels grow cold over the whole body at unchaste or extra-marriage love.
Next spoke those who were in cold and heat; in cold towards their wives, and in heat towards the sex...

Those who love natural things only... cannot be conjoined with their consort as into one, except as to those externals; and when these fail, cold invades the internals, which disperses the delights of that love...
Marriage love grows cold as soon as it is divided; and this coldness causes it to perish.

If wives were to say that they love... cold would invade their husbands, and would separate from bed, chamber, and look; but this takes place with those who do not regard marriages as holy, and therefore do not love their wives from spiritual love: it is otherwise with those who do.
(When the inspiration of love from the female sex was cut off, the men became completely cold.)

Marriage cold is deeply seated in most men... If wives were to disclose the affections and inclinations of their husbands, this cold would burst forth from its hiding places, and would first chill the interiors of the minds, then the breast, and thence the ultimates of love...
The intermissions of marriage love with those married partners who love each other only exteriorly are not from the same causes; but from alternate cold and heat. Explained.

The inclinations and affections of men grow cold towards their wives, while the husbands think vain things against the Lord and the Church; they grow cold while they are in conceit from their own intelligence; they grow cold while they regard strange women with concupiscence; they grow cold while the subject of love is adverted to by their wives; they, moreover, grow cold with a varied cold... If the men are cold to their wives it is ill with them...
With those who (are not in true marriage love), and who do not think of separation, love remains in the externals, but is cold in the internals.
On the causes of colds, etc., in marriages. Chapter.
Opposites induce cold to one, if not to both.
There is spiritual heat, and there is spiritual cold; and spiritual heat is love, and spiritual cold is the deprivation thereof. General article.

Spiritual cold is from the sun of the natural world, and from its heat and light... When natural heat is separated from spiritual heat, as is the case with those who love natural things, and reject spiritual, spiritual heat becomes cold.

Merely natural Spirits are chilled with intense cold, when they apply themselves to the side of some Angel who is in a state of love; and it is the same with the Spirits of Hell when heat from Heaven inflows to them.

Spiritual cold in marriages is disunion of souls, and disjunction of minds; whence come indifference, discord, contempt, loathing, aversion; from which with many comes separation as to bed, chamber, and house. General article.

Marriage cold resides over all other colds in human minds; for the marriage principle itself is inscribed on the soul... Hence it is that this cold commences there, and successively descends into the consequents, and infects them...
The causes of colds in their successions are many; some internal, some external, and some accidental. General article.
The internal causes of colds are from religion. General article.
Where there is no marriage love, there is cold... Marriage cold is also the privation of the state of the Church, or of religion.
The first of the internal causes of colds, is the rejection of religion by both. General article.
Such, as to marriage love, are chilled with cold more than all others.
The second of the internal causes of colds, is that one has religion and not the other. General article.

When marriage love is banished, there ensues cold; but this with the married partner of no religion: this cold is not dissipated except through the reception of a religion which agrees with that of the other, if the latter is a true one; otherwise, with the married partner who has no religion, there ensues cold, which descends from the soul into the body, even to the cuticles...
The third of the internal causes of colds, is that one is of one religion, and the other of another. General article.
Hence with the married partner who is in falsities of religion there commences cold, which is intensified in proportion as he differs from the other.
The fourth of the internal causes (of cold), is falsity of religion. General article.
The above-named causes are causes of internal cold, but, with many, not at the same time of external. General article.

If the causes which are causes of cold in internals were to produce a similar cold in externals, there would be as many separations as there are internal colds; and there are as many colds as there are marriages of those who are in falsity of religion, in different religions, and in no religion.
There are many causes which conjoin dispositions, but which do not conjoin souls... but still cold lies hidden inwardly, and causes itself to be noticed and felt every now and then...
The external causes of cold are also many; and the first of these is dissimilitude of dispositions and manners. General article.
The second of the external causes of cold, is that marriage love is believed to be one with scortatory love, except that the latter is not allowed by law. General article.
For nothing stores up in itself marriage cold more than scortatory love; and as it passes into it, it may not undeservedly be called marriage cold itself.
The third of the external causes (of cold), is a striving for pre-eminence between married partners. General article.
The fourth of the external causes of cold, is no determination to any study or business; whence comes wandering cupidity. General article.
With these, marriage cold is different from that cold with others; it is indeed the privation of marriage love, but from defect.
The fifth of the external causes (of cold), is inequality of state and condition in external things. General article.
The accidental causes of cold are also many; and the first of these is what is common from being constantly allowed. General article.
The second of the accidental causes of cold, is that living with a married partner from covenant and law seems compulsory, and not free. General article.

This cause exists only with those with whom marriage love is cold in the inmosts, and as it adds itself to inward cold, it becomes an accessory or accidental cause: with these, extra-marriage love is in heat; for the cold of the one is the heat of the other; which, if not felt, is still in it; nay, in the midst of cold; otherwise there would be no reparation.
The third of the accidental causes of cold is affirmation by the wife, and a talking about love by her. General article.
The fourth of the accidental causes of cold, is the man's thought by day and night that his wife is willing; and on the other hand, the wife's thought that the man is not willing. General article.
As cold is in the mind so it is in the body; and according to the increasings of that cold, the externals of the body too are closed. General article.
I was thinking deeply... in what region of the mind... does marriage cold reside?

Marriage cold too dwells in the highest region of the mind; but only in the chamber of the understanding; that of the will being then closed; for the understanding with its truths can ascend as often as it likes by a winding stair into its chamber in the highest region, but if the will with the good of its love does not ascend at the same time into the consociate chamber, the latter is closed, and cold ensues in the other, and this is marriage cold. While there is such cold towards the wife, the understanding, from the highest region, looks downwards to the lowest one, and also, if not held back by fear, descends, in order to warm itself there at an illicit fire.

Marriage love with the spiritual married partner is heat, and with the natural one is cold; and it is evident that heat and cold cannot be together, and that heat cannot kindle him who is in cold unless this be first dispelled; nor can cold flow into him who is in heat unless this he first removed.
But between two natural married partners no inward love can exist, because both are cold...
As heats communicate with each other, so do colds...
While the men are in the alternate colds, let them not consider their wives as beneath their maidservants.

With every man who is not spiritually, but only naturally rational and moral, there is cold towards a wife; this cold lies hidden with him in the inmosts: this a wise and sagacious wife observes exquisitely and acutely, and in the same degree she conceals her marriage love... The reason is, that in proportion as it appears, the marriage cold of the man pours forth from the inmosts of his mind into the ultimates, and induces a total coldness on the body... I then asked, Whence comes such cold, as you call marriage cold? They replied, It is from their insanity in spiritual things; for everyone who is insane in spiritual things, is inmostly cold to a wife, and inmostly warm to harlots; and as marriage love and scortatory love are opposite to each other, it follows that marriage love becomes cold while scortatory love is heat; and that when cold reigns with a man he cannot endure any sense of love, and thus not any afflatus of it, from his wife.
As in the beginning it was all on fire, so its fire suddenly goes out, and passes off into the cold of winter; whence defect is accelerated.
If the successive order of this love is precipitated... there thence arises cold for marriage...
As many unchastenesses, so many colds; and so many as there are of the latter, so many obstructions are there of the inmost life... whence the spring is dried up.
If the intelligence of the man does not unite itself with its own genuine love, which is with the wife... marriage love becomes cold. What woman can unite her love to cold?
With adulterers, virility is weakened even to nothing; and then there commences cold even to the sex... CL 453.
Evil is in the cold of Hell, and falsity is in its thick darkness.
In the frigid zones in the Spiritual World there are the same appearances as in the frigid zones in the natural world. Described. SE 5144.

Whenever those approached who had separated faith from charity, such cold seized my feet, and successively my loins and my breast, that everything vital of my body would have been extinguished unless the Lord had driven those Spirits away... Yet those Spirits felt no cold in themselves; wherefore I compared them to fish under the ice, which likewise feel no cold, as their life and thence their nature is in itself cold. I perceived that that cold emanated from the deceptive light of their faith...
Faith without charity is dead... and its death is from the cold; from which faith expires like a bird in a severe winter...
The man who believes regeneration to be possible without any free will in spiritual things, thus without cooperation, becomes as cold as a stone as to all the truths of the Church...
Melancthon appears clothed with a hairy skin, because faith without charity is cold.
That the lower place of damnation [i.e., of vastation] is very cold.
In the bodily life they had been cold, having been imbued with no true love, but only with the pleasures of the body...
The inmost joy of one... was nothing but cold...
That I was surrounded by such a diabolical crew... I plainly felt from a coldish wind whenever they were assembled...
That the states of the spiritual things of man's life are also represented in the other life by cold and heat.

They who have led a life of the body, or one of the love of the world and of self, are cold as to the degrees and varieties of every state; and indeed so cold that when they approached they struck my limbs with cold, and also with cold blasts...
On the cold of those who are of the devil's crew.

Whenever there have approached any of the diabolical crew, whether few or many, I have been seized with cold in a greater or less degree in various parts of the body; round the head, at the ears, round the body, at the feet: I could tell when they came from the cold, and also from the breathing, which was usually cold.
On my asking whether he was cold; he replied that he was not warm, although he appeared fiery. SE 549. SE 629.
(They who acknowledge God the Father only) after death are cold, and seek to obtain warmth by sawing grass into very little pieces.
A certain one of the very learned... was cold, as I plainly felt from his cold afflatus...

The life of his faith flowed in, as I could plainly perceive by this; that I began to doubt or feel coldly respecting the Lord's government in singulars... The cold was that of his intellectual faith, or of truths, but not so much of affection.
I felt the coming of (the assassin); he was now cold; thus was among the cold infernals.
(The inhabitants of Saturn) do not suffer from cold; thus have no concern about garments.
A certain rather cold breathing on my forehead (from those Spirits of the dura mater).
Wherever these Spirits (who constitute the spurious animal spirits) go, they stiffen all other things; they induce cold on them...
I could not perceive the heat of those who are delighted with the more interior things of the Word; wherefore I felt something of cold in externals.

Certain Spirits celebrated the feast of tabernacles; but as they did it from mere cupidity, without any view of interior things, their delight was turned into sadness and into cold, which was communicated to my feet and knees; for they desired only natural things... thence came the cold: certain Spirits also complained of the cold: such is the case with merely natural gladnesses.
Cold and heat felt from Spirits; cold the more frequently.

When the interior Spirits of the World of Spirits flow in even only a little, there is at once perceived a cold or weariness towards those things which are of the Lord's Word, of faith, and of salvation...
So far as they place merit in themselves, they grow cold.

When Sirens approach the celestial things of love, thus towards Heaven, they become cold; as cold as snow and ice. They can become both fire and ice, and thus undulate from one extreme to the other; so that they are miserably tortured.

A certain preacher together with his like said that their life consisted in their being nothing: they did not admit any knowledges of faith, hardly the terms faith and love, except from the bodily sense of love; for they suppose that marriages in common are allowable: their life was perceived to be cold... the cold seizing on the hands, the left knee, and the foot even to the sole. SE 3434. SE 3444.
Through the removal of imperfections, as of those things which cause weight, rest, cold...

The life of business of the Dutch was represented as a life of wintry light; I felt much cold therefrom in the foot and knee. I was let into that light, and at the same time into the state in which they are when all their business succeeds; they then said that they were in their Heaven; but the cold of that life was felt round the left part of the head; they, however, did not feel the cold, but a heat, which, when communicated to me, affected the left part of the forehead and the left knee. But their heat is turned into frost. SE 3522.

The life of cupidities is as it were fiery, and the life of reasoning is as the lumen thence; but on the approach of the life of love the fire is dulled and extinguished, and at last is turned into cold, and the lumen into darkness.

I felt a great cold from the soles of the feet, and through the feet into the loins, and I perceived that it was Spirits who were rising up who were thus cold, or rather frozen: they were those who as to externals had lived as beasts, and supposed that they would die like beasts; but they were vivified by the Lord through Angels. Afterwards I also felt cold from them, but verging to heat. SE 3555.
There are also Spirits... who infuse colds, and thereby the paroxysms of ague... SE 4591.
(Spirits) have an idea of heat and cold, but only from the state of the life.
To give a drink of cold water = to exercise charity from obedience.

Thou art neither cold nor hot = that being without charity it is between Heaven and Hell. Cold = those who are not in spiritual love but in infernal love... Hence to be neither cold nor hot = that it is in neither infernal love nor spiritual love, but between both; and he who is between both is between Heaven and Hell.
The reason cold = infernal love, is that heat = heavenly love.
Would thou wert cold or hot = that it is better there should be no faith, or that there should be charity alone.
He who is cold, that is, without faith, does not profane.
Snow = cold truths.
The strange cold flowing waters () = falsities in which there is no good; strange waters = falsities; and cold = in which there is no good, for truths derive all their heat from the good of love.
Who can stand before His cold? () = man's state before reformation.

The scientifics and Knowledges which are with man before reformation are signified by hail like balls, who can stand before His cold? (); for before reformation man is completely cold, and that cold is manifestly felt when the Divine flows in from Heaven; and as these colds are dissipated through the reception of Divine good and Divine truth, thus through reformation, it is said,He sendeth forth His Word, and melteth them: He causeth His wind to blow, and the waters flow.

Aversion to truths is signified by cold in the night (); for when the light of Heaven, which in its essence is Divine truth, flows in, they who are in falsities from evil are seized with cold, intense according to the warmth of the falsity from evil.
Cold = the deprivation of the good of love.
The day of cold () = a state of the love of evil.
To give to drink a cup of cold water = to teach from a little innocence.

To give to drink a cup of cold water in the name of a disciple = from obedience to do good and teach truth; for water = truth in affection; and cold water, truth in obedience; for mere obedience is a natural and not a spiritual affection, wherefore it is relatively cold.
